liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing In/The Band** (3 reviews): Reviewer praises Jerry's wah-pedal work in Playin' in the Band; Reviewer treats Playing in the Band as a mind-bending piece worth long study [11][12][19]
- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Dark Star is rated very good, notable since that era isn't known for strong versions; Adventurous yet accessible Dark Star, though Phil goes too far out near the end for this reviewer [9][11][19]
- **Loser** (1 review): Named among the best-executed songs of the night [10]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Singled out as especially well executed, along with Loser and the Weather Report Suite into Let It Grow [10]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Laid-back China into Rider, with a jam in the middle and bright Jerry notes [18]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): A nice Uncle John's Band riff appears in the middle of I Know You Rider [19]
- **Weather Report Suite Prelude** (1 review): Weather Report Suite Prelude into Part 1 and Let It Grow is the best version this reviewer has heard, with a funny conversation with Jerry at the start [17]

## Setlist highlights

- **Let Me Sing Your Blues Away**: rare: 8 archived performances [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-09-11.120143.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 194 min; rated 4.9/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: On the soundboard master, numerous pops appear in the left channel and some in the right [1]
- **gd73-09-11.sbd.lanum.184.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 178 min; rated 4.37/5 by 52 [4]. Said about its sound: Sound quality described as crisp and excellent; Reviewer can't hear the horns until Let It Grow, despite the database saying they start earlier; Audio is exceptional apart from some minor pops and cracks [11][16][17]
- **gd1973-09-11.116231.aud.warburton.berger.cousinit-patched.flac16**: audience recording; 22 songs; 196 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1973-09-11.112220.aud.warburton.berger-patched.flac16**: audience recording; 22 songs; 196 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says it was a birthday in the band, and the group had a good night [10]
- Reviewer notes one of Phil Lesh's rare solos, plus horns and short country tunes [12]
- Doug Sahm's band opened, and its sax player joined the band on Weather Report [13]
- Near 2:00 am, Bobby announced the band enjoyed itself so much they would return the next night [13]
- Reviewer was a freshman at W&M during orientation week and attended this show [13]
- Reviewer says this is the first of eight shows with horns; database says horns begin at Weather Report Suite [16]
- Reviewer notes September 11th is Mickey Hart's birthday [20]
- Doug Sahm opened; Martin Fierro and Joe Ellis played horns on Let Me Sing, Weather Report Suite and Let It Grow [1]
- Reviewer points to the 3/28/73 show as a related favorite [12]
- Reviewer says it's perhaps not a top ten show but holds its own against strong 1973 competition [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-09-11.120143.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by matrix by dusborne; source: 2 source matrix: SBD: MR>C1>DAT>Goodbear_Edit>CD (shnid=113051) and Original Audience Source: (shnid=116231) Jimmy Warburton's reel [1]
- **gd73-09-11.sbd.lanum.184.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1973-09-11.116231.aud.warburton.berger.cousinit-patched.flac16**: transferred by Rob Berger;Cousinit;Jimmy Warburton; source: Original source: AUD Jimmy Warburton's reel; [2]
- **gd1973-09-11.112220.aud.warburton.berger-patched.flac16**: transferred by Rob Berger; source: source: aud; Jimmy Warburton's reel; [3]
